To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the R1/m law is a good approximation for the radial luminosity profile of galaxies and that the structural and dynamical parameters are well described by the asymptotic expressions for large and small radii, which can be used for the analysis of the properties of galaxies.
the R 1/2 -law models are not stable and that the R 3/2 -law model is unstable.
the R 1/2 and R 1/3 models are the most realistic ones for the description of the stellar systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structural and dynamical features of isotropic spherical stellar systems with luminosity density following a R1/m-law.
the following questions: (1) How does the structure of a galaxy depend on the luminosity law?
the following questions: What is the effect of the surface luminosity profile R 1/m law on the structural and dynamical parameters of stellar systems?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for m < 5.5, the R 1 /m law is a good description for spherical galaxies with a flat rotation curve.
, in general, the R1/m law is a good representation of the surface luminosity profile for galaxies, but not for clusters of galaxies.
the R 1/4 law is a good approximation for the luminosity distribution of galaxies, but it is not the only possible law, as the R 1/n law with n = 4 is a special case of the more general R 1/m law.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the R 1/2 -law is the only one for which the asymptotic behavior of the luminosity density is the same for both small and large radi, while for the other laws the asymptotic luminosity density is different for the two limits.
for the R 1/10 -law the models are not very different from the isothermal sphere.
the R 1/2 -law is the only surface luminosity profile that can be used to describe isotropic spherical galaxies, and that the R 3/2 -law can be safely discarded.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the R 1/10 law is the most natural choice, in the sense that the models are more compact and have more centrally concentrated luminosity and velocity dispersion profiles, and the velocity dispersion profiles are less sensitive to changes in the central potential.
for a wide range of m values the models can reproduce the observed properties of the Milky Way, M31 and M33 galaxies.
, for a given value of the mass density parameter, the models with m = 2 and m = 10 are the ones that better reproduce, respectively, the inner and outer regions of the luminosity density profile.
